communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Initial-contract (CBM) cases and their outcomes, October 1999 to present
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please include all cases with N-Category "Initial Contract" (Case Type CBM) opened or received from October 1, 1999 through the date the search is run, whatever the case's status or reason for closing. That means cases closed with "Agreement Reached" and also, for example:

- "Parties Failed to Respond"
- "Case Cancelled"
- "Question re: Representation"
- "Employees Included In/Folded Into Existing Unit"
- "Facility Closed"
- "Other"
- cases with no reason for closing recorded
- cases still open

My earlier request FOIA-2022-00042 was fulfilled with only cases closed as "Agreement Reached".

For this request I am asking that cases which did not reach agreement can be counted.

Fields. For each case, please provide the following, where they exist. Field names are from the extract produced for FOIA-2022-00042:
1. The FMCS case number or other unique case identifier
2. Received Date; Initiated Date; the date the case was closed
3. Case Type; N-Case Type; N-Category; N-Case Source (for example F-7 from Union, F-7 from Organization, NLRB, FLRA)
4. N-Date Submitted, and any identifier linking the case to its F-7 notice
5. The NLRB case number (for example 13-RC-123456), or the certification date, for cases opened from NLRB certifications
6. Basis for Closing (Case Statistics)
7. Contract Agreement Date
8. Employer; Union; Union Local; bargaining unit size (BU)
9. The employer's location and the affected or bargaining-unit location (city, state, ZIP code)
10. The industry code (NAICS), if recorded
11. Whether a mediator held joint or separate meetings, and the number and dates of those meetings, if recorded

Personal information. To make processing easier, you may leave out the names, telephone numbers and email addresses of individual employer and union contacts. I do not need them. Please do not leave out the employer or union names.

Older records. If cases from before a particular year are in a legacy system, or have fewer fields, please provide whatever is available for those years, and tell me which fields or years are missing rather than withholding the rest.

Format. I would like the records as a spreadsheet or delimited text file (.xlsx or .csv), one row per case, in the form the system exports. If producing all years would take much longer, please send each portion as it becomes ready, starting with the most recent years.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Forest Gregg

communications.subject: Ohio Open Records Law Request: The Ohio State University Marching Band
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Ohio Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Ohio Public Records Act (Ohio Revised Code Section 149.43), I hereby request the following records:

Any records detailing the annual operating budgets and financial allocations for The Ohio State University Marching Band, spanning the time frame from January 2023 through October 2026.

communications.subject: Pennsylvania Right to Know Act Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Pennsylvania Right to Know Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

Dillion,

Pursuant to 1 MRS §408-A(3) the MSP acknowledges FOAA request as outlined below. Pursuant to Public Law 113-242 section 2 states that the State shall report to the Attorney General, on a quarterly basis and pursuant to guidelines established by the Attorney General, information regarding the death of any person who is detained, under arrest, or is in the process of being arrested, is enroute to be incarcerated, or is incarcerated at a municipal or county jail, State prison, State-run boot camp prison, boot camp prison that is contracted out by the State, any State or local contract facility, or other local or state correctional facility (including any juvenile facility). The Office of the Attorney General is responsible for investigating and reviewing such cases in Maine (5 MRS §200-A).
